question: A group of scientists is conducting an experiment on the human cells involved in the immune response. They genetically modify B cells so they do not express the cluster of differentiation 21 (CD21) on their cell surfaces. The pathogenesis of which of the following organisms would most likely be affected by this genetic modification?
analysis: CD21, also known as complement receptor 2 (CR2), is a receptor on B cells that is used by the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) to infect these cells. By genetically modifying B cells to not express CD21, the entry of EBV into these cells would be hindered, affecting its pathogenesis. Other viruses listed, such as measles virus, HIV, human papillomavirus, and parvovirus B19, do not primarily use CD21 for cell entry.
